question: Can a parity scorecard cell read GREEN on a test that never exercises the property it claims to measure -- and how many do?
discriminator: A cell is EXERCISED when the ptrace-golden stdout differs from the BARE-HOST stdout. If the bare host already produces the golden bytes, hermit changed nothing observable, so no backend can fail the cell and parity=1 asserts coverage that does not exist.
why_bare_exec: hermit has NO `native` backend -- `--backend` accepts only ptrace/dbi/liteinst/sabre/kvm/e9patch -- so the do-nothing control must bypass hermit entirely. A prior design note asserted `backend_available("native")==true`; that is refuted.
not_established: cpuid_probe's NO-PAYLOAD is an artifact of MY flag choice: --no-virtualize-cpuid defeats the very identity that fixture asserts, so it exits nonzero and emits nothing. It is not evidence about that cell.

NOT-EXERCISED is a statement about the STDOUT-PARITY metric the scorecard uses, not a claim that the fixture is worthless: several of these fixtures branch internally and would exit nonzero on a wrong answer. The parity CELL still cannot distinguish a determinizing backend from an inert one.
Scope is the backend-parity-c fixture family (82 guests), not the full 618-row scorecard. The mechanism is wired for every cell; only this family was swept.
